post.description: Use for who is buying whom, at what price, and whether the deal is pending or closed. For the coverage and commentary around a deal use news/search.

parameters[tickers].description: Comma-separated ticker symbols, maximum 50. Set this when the caller asks whether a named company is acquiring or being acquired.

parameters[date].description: A single date, YYYY-MM-DD, as shorthand when date_from and date_to would be the same. Leave unset to get the latest deals.

parameters[date_from].description: Earliest date, YYYY-MM-DD, interpreted against date_sort.

parameters[date_to].description: Latest date, YYYY-MM-DD, interpreted against date_sort.

parameters[date_sort].description:
Which deal date to sort on. Use announced for a chronology of new deals, expected for pending closes, or completed for deals that have closed.

Provider reference: allowed values ["expected", "completed", "announced"].

parameters[importance].description:
Minimum importance level, matched as greater than or equal to the value given. Raise it when the caller only wants large or notable deals.

Provider reference: allowed values ["0", "1", "2", "3", "4", "5"].

parameters[updated].description: Unix timestamp in UTC; returns only records updated at or after it. Set this when polling for changes since a previous call.

page.description:
Zero-based page offset, capped at 100000. Prefer narrowing by date over paging deep.

Provider reference: maximum 100000; default 0.

pagesize.description:
Number of records to return, limit 1000.

Provider reference: maximum 1000.

post.description: Use for how analysts have moved on a stock: upgrades, downgrades, initiations and target changes. Filter by parameters[analyst_id] or parameters[firm_id] to follow one analyst or firm. It carries the ratings, not the reasoning behind them.

fields.description: Comma-separated response fields to return, or * for every field including ratings_accuracy. Available: id, date, time, ticker, exchange, name, currency, action_pt, action_company, rating_current, pt_current, rating_prior, pt_prior, pt_pct_change, url, url_calendar, url_news, analyst, analyst_id, analyst_name, firm_id, ratings_accuracy, importance, notes, updated. Set it to trim the payload when you only need the rating and target.

parameters[firm_id].description: Comma-separated firm ids. Take them from the id field of calendar/ratings-firms, or the firm_id on a rating, to keep to one research firm's coverage.

parameters[action].description:
Ratings action to filter to, matched against action_company.

Provider reference: allowed values ["Assumes", "Downgrades", "Firm Dissolved", "Initiates Coverage On", "Maintains", "Reinstates", "Reiterates", "Removes", "Suspends", "Terminates Coverage On", "Upgrades"].

parameters[importance].description:
Minimum importance level, matched as greater than or equal to the value given. Raise it when the caller only wants the notable calls.

Provider reference: allowed values ["0", "1", "2", "3", "4", "5"].

parameters[updated].description: Unix timestamp. Returns records updated at or after it, for polling deltas.

Page offset, 0 to 100000.

Provider reference: maximum 100000; default 0.

Records to return. Limit 1000.

post.description: Use to resolve an analyst by name, or to judge how accurate a particular analyst has been, and to get the id you then pass to calendar/ratings as parameters[analyst_id]. For the ratings themselves use calendar/ratings; for the list of firms rather than people use calendar/ratings-firms.

page.description:
Page offset, limited to 0-100000. Set this only when walking past the first page of the analyst roster.

Provider reference: default 0.

pageSize.description:
Number of analysts to return, limit 1000. Raise it when you want the roster in one call rather than paging.

Provider reference: maximum 1000; default 100.

fields.description: Comma-separated list of response fields to return. Set it to trim the payload when you only need names and ids and not the ratings_accuracy block.

analyst.description: Analyst identifier to look up. Set this when you already have an analyst_id from a ratings record and want that analyst's profile and accuracy.

analyst_name.description: Analyst name to match. Set this when the caller names a person rather than supplying an id; the reference does not say whether matching is exact, so try the full name first.

firm.description: Firm identifier to restrict to. Set this to list only the analysts working at one research firm.

firm_name.description: Firm name to match. Use it when the caller names the bank, for example Morgan Stanley, instead of supplying a firm id.

updated.description: Unix timestamp (UTC); only records updated at or after this are returned, and the sort order follows it. Set this to poll for roster changes since your last sync.

post.description: Use this for company-issued announcements as distributed over the wires (PRNewswire, Globe Newswire, Business Wire, ACCESS Newswire, Newsfile), the primary-source wording behind a story, including licensing, collaboration and acquisition deals with the upfront, milestone and total values the companies disclosed. For a subject rather than a company, pass topics with topic_group_by and (for example license agreement,upfront payment) plus dateFrom and dateTo, and displayOutput full to quote the terms. For Benzinga editorial coverage and the wider newswire use news/search, and for the one-line explanation of a price move use news/wiims.

page.description:
Page offset, limited to 0-100000. Increase it to page past the first batch rather than widening the date range.

Provider reference: default 0.

pageSize.description:
Number of releases returned, maximum 100. Raise it when you want a full day of a company's releases in one call.

Provider reference: maximum 100; default 15.

displayOutput.description:
How much of each release to return: headline only, abstract (headline plus teaser) or full body text. Set full only when you need to quote the release.
